title: Objective Trajectory Router and Contingency Crediting
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: company-level OKRs are currently translated into many disparate initiatives with brittle handoffs at quarter boundaries. Resource contention and ad-hoc rollbacks cause repeated rework. Objective Trajectory Router (OTR) is a lightweight decision layer that maps OKR trajectories (target, leading indicators, risk vector) to initiative lanes and a small pool of contingency credits that can be reallocated across teams when blockers / regressions occur.
goal: Create an operational model and tooling prototype that (1) makes OKR->initiative routing explicit, (2) exposes a short-term contingency credit pool and gating rules, and (3) provides dashboards and comms templates so PMs and Eng leads can reassign credits quickly without breaking delivery commitments.
approach: Phase 1: Design the routing rules and crediting policy (policy repo + playbook). Phase 2: Prototype a simple Rails/Next microservice + dashboard that surfaces trajectory conflicts and suggests credit moves. Phase 3: Pilot across two cross-functional initiatives (Console + Dedicated). Integrate with Linear for automated signals and with Console telemetry for latency/cost tradeoffs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Routing rules documented and reviewed by GTM/Eng leaders.
2) Credit pool semantics implemented in prototype and can be reassigned with an audit trail.
3) Pilot shows at least one successful credit reallocation that avoids a rollback.
4) Dashboard surfaces OKR-initiative mismatches and projected impact within 24 hours of signal.
risks:
- Risk: perceived centralization of decision rights; mitigate by explicit roles & SLAs in playbook.
- Risk: gamification of credit pool; mitigate with audit logs and quarterly reconciliation.
- Risk: tooling scope creep; mitigate by keeping MVP feature-limited (routing + audit + comms templates).
metrics: Primary: number of mid-quarter rollbacks avoided (goal: >=1 in pilot), time to decision for credit reallocation (goal: <8 hours), PM/Eng satisfaction score for alignment (survey target >=4/5). Secondary: change in initiative completion velocity and OKR indicator delta.
